parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence or universal facility/document rule is documented, but the structural picture extrapolates badly. An enforced criminal statute (raids, convictions, 'gay appearance' as evidence) gives police an active lever against gender-nonconforming people; NGOs record arrests but not trans shares, so exposure is unmeasured, not absent. Most damning: vigilante killings, beatings and torture of people read as gender-nonconforming with police complicity or indifference, and no functioning recourse — tier-2-to-3 exposure with severity up to lethal violence. De facto criminalisation of gender-affirming care, no recognition route, no advocacy space, openly negative social climate, and an official asylum assessment that trans women face societal difficulties even with relocation. Thin trans-specific record resolves toward the risk the enforced statute and police-complicit violence imply, slightly above the gang-targeting 0.25 anchors in hostility but below the 0.15 tier for lack of documented near-automatic imprisonment or targeting of trans identity itself.
